correctness.rationale: Read frozen RESULT.md and METADATA.json, independently reconstructed the divisor identity a(2^k m)=((2^(k+1)-3)σ(m)-λ(m))/4 for k>=1, m odd and the bound 0<=λ(m)<=τ(m). For k>=2, m=1 attains 2^(k-1)-1; among m>1, m=3 attains 2^(k+1)-3, and m>3 gives strict inequality because σ(m)-τ(m)>=m-1>=4 and C_k>1. For odd m, prime, higher-prime-power and two-prime-factor cases rigorously exclude all further a(m)<5; doubling a(2m)=a(m), and dyadic bounds limit k>=2 to 4,8. Independently computed signed q-series and divisor sums for n<=100 and checked fibers; no finite test used to infer the global theorem.
